summary: The lecture begins with the loss of the ustaz's mentor, Datuk Dr. Madeline Berma, and goes on to the etiquette of condolences to families of other faiths and the nature of the Hereafter. The ustaz then tells of the death of Khadijah RA, the wife in whom the Prophet SAW found refuge through the hardest years, from the boycott, to Allah's greeting through Jibril, to her burial. He then shows how memories of Khadijah kept stirring the Prophet SAW, such as the ransom necklace of Abul Az, Hala's voice, the old woman he honoured, and Aisyah's jealousy. This is tied to the experience of losing a spouse today, books, films and the importance of a peaceful home, and ends with the Prophet SAW returning to Makkah as its conqueror and spending the night at Hujun, where Khadijah was buried.
keyPoints: We cannot be sure of anyone's fate in the Hereafter; offer condolences and good prayers without passing judgment, and the istirja' phrase may be used in every situation.
Khadijah RA was the first to believe in the Prophet SAW, stayed loyal through the boycott though she was not of Bani Hashim, and was where the Prophet found calm.
Allah sent Khadijah His greeting through Jibril and promised her a house of pearl in Paradise with no noise and no fatigue, the two things she bore in this world.
The Prophet SAW never forgot Khadijah: the ransom necklace, Hala's voice and the old woman who used to visit them all revived memories, and he honoured Khadijah's friends.
Grief for a spouse lasts long and is often triggered again, so we should be sensitive in comforting and not turn death into social media content.
A home should be a place free of noise and fatigue, and one bad moment does not define a couple's whole journey.

chapters.title: Opening and returning after a long break
chapters.summary: The lecture opens with a picture of the Prophet SAW's grief, then the ustaz explains his preparation and why classes were postponed.

chapters.title: Dr. Madeline Berma's message and relations with those of other faiths
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls the death of Abu Talib and his mentor's last message about helping the poor and understanding the stories of those who fall.

chapters.title: Condolences and the fate in the Hereafter
chapters.summary: With Surah At-Tawbah verse 113 and the hadith of the martyr who showed off, the ustaz stresses we do not judge anyone's end, and the istirja' phrase may be used for all.

chapters.title: The date of Khadijah's death and the Prophet's emotional graph
chapters.summary: Scholars agree Khadijah died in the same year as Abu Talib, and the Prophet SAW had long carried grief that was nearing its lowest point.

chapters.title: Khadijah in the boycott and the Prophet's love for her
chapters.summary: Khadijah joined the nearly three-year boycott though not of Bani Hashim, and the Prophet SAW's love for her was never matched.

chapters.title: Allah's greeting and glad tidings through Jibril
chapters.summary: The hadith in which Jibril brings Allah's greeting and the promise of a pearl house without noise or fatigue to Khadijah.

chapters.title: The burial of Khadijah RA
chapters.summary: Khadijah died in Ramadan of the tenth year of prophethood and was buried at Hujun, the Prophet SAW himself going down into the grave.

chapters.title: The Prophet's grief after her death
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW stayed home and was not seen smiling for a long time, and replied to Khawlah by remembering Khadijah's goodness.

chapters.title: Death as a reminder, not social media content
chapters.summary: The ustaz rebukes the habit of filming and taking selfies at funerals, and tells of his teacher's wish for no photos or videos.

chapters.title: Buya Hamka and books on grief
chapters.summary: Buya Hamka's life after his wife's death and two books by Asma' Hussein show grief lasts, and words of comfort must be chosen with care.

chapters.title: Memories that stirred the Prophet: Badr and Khadijah's necklace
chapters.summary: Memories of Khadijah stirred the Prophet even in war, when he recognised the necklace sent as Abul Az's ransom.

chapters.title: Hala's voice and the old woman who was Khadijah's friend
chapters.summary: Hala's voice reminded the Prophet of Khadijah, and he honoured an old woman who used to visit them as a sign of faith.

chapters.title: Memories in times of ease and Aisyah's jealousy
chapters.summary: The Prophet remembered those who were with him in hardship, and Aisyah herself told of her jealousy and his reply that Allah did not replace Khadijah with anyone better.

chapters.title: Film and book recommendations
chapters.summary: The ustaz recommends the films Imaginur and Habibie and Ainun, and Salman Al-Audah's book that reflects on Jibril's hadith.

chapters.title: A home of peace and one moment that does not define us
chapters.summary: A home should be free of noise and fatigue, and a last quarrel does not decide a couple's whole journey.

chapters.title: The Prophet's loyalty, return to Makkah and closing
chapters.summary: The Prophet did not marry another during Khadijah's life, returned to Makkah as a conqueror and camped at Hujun, and the ustaz closes with recommended books and the hadith on bringing joy to a grieving heart.

books.context: The ustaz reads a passage that Khadijah died three days after Abu Talib and filled the Prophet's heart with sakinah, mawaddah and rahmah. The book is also cited for Khadijah's grave at Hujun.
A book by an archaeologist who found Khadijah's house during the expansion of the Masjid Al-Haram, with sketches of the house's size and position.
The ustaz cites Ibn Hisham's narration of Khadijah testing whether the visitor was an angel, and a tense dialogue about Al-Lat and Al-Uzza.
books.note: Title given by the ustaz as the narration of Ibn Hisham

books.context: A classic sirah book that says the Prophet SAW did not leave his house or meet people for a long time after Khadijah died.
books.note: Full title not mentioned in the lecture: At-Tabaqat Al-Kubra

books.context: Written by Buya Hamka's son about his father after the death of his wife Siti Raham, and also about Hamka's life as scholar, writer and head of the family.
The reflections of a young widow from Egypt whose husband was shot in the face while protesting, on six years of grieving.
The second book by the same author; both were reviewed by scholars and hold many triggers of memory and lessons in sensitivity to those who grieve.
A 90-minute Malaysian film that repeats itself and confuses, but moves at the end on the feeling of losing a beloved wife; the script was co-written with Reza Minhad.
A film about Bapak Habibie, former Prime Minister of Indonesia, and his wife Ainun. The ustaz also recommends watching his real interviews, in which he always spoke of his wife.

A sirah reflection with a chapter on making the marriage home a place without noise and fatigue, based on Jibril's hadith to Khadijah. According to the ustaz, the author has been imprisoned since 2017.
books.note: Title given by the ustaz as Ma'al Musbafa

books.context: Based on authentic sources but written in the style of a novel, bought by the ustaz as a gift for his wife.
A slim, practical book available free online, from the ustaz's teacher. The author also has a lecture series of around 19 hours.
A biography of the Prophet SAW built on early sources, suited to reading the years of Khadijah's and Abu Talib's deaths.
A concise, well-ordered sirah book that covers the Year of Sorrow.

lessons.title: Do not judge others' fate in the Hereafter
lessons.body: We cannot be certain of anyone's end, Muslims included, except what was revealed to the prophets.

lessons.title: Be humble about our fate in the Hereafter
lessons.body: The hadith of the first three groups into the Fire tells us not to be overconfident and to always hope for Allah's mercy.

lessons.title: Courteous condolences to families of another faith
lessons.body: Offer condolences and kind words so they are granted patience, and the istirja' phrase suits every situation.

lessons.title: Grief lasts longer than the first days
lessons.body: The heavier part is after people return to routine and we feel no one remembers any more.

lessons.title: Death is a reminder, not content
lessons.body: At a funeral, reflect on the end and avoid filming or taking selfies, as Shaykh Muhammad Al-Sharif asked.

lessons.title: Be careful with words of comfort
lessons.body: Saying Allah will replace it with something better may hurt someone still grieving, so their feelings need understanding.

lessons.title: Memories can always stir grief
lessons.body: The bereaved do not simply move on, because a smell, a voice or a place can bring memories back, like the necklace and Hala's voice for the Prophet SAW.

lessons.title: Keep ties with the friends of those who have gone
lessons.body: Keeping up with the friends and family of someone we love after they die is part of faith.

lessons.title: Remember those who were with us in hardship
lessons.body: In times of ease, the Prophet SAW and the Companions remembered those who did not live to see it, and shared gifts and food.

lessons.title: Be thankful for a spouse's love
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW said he was granted Khadijah's love, though Khadijah herself was grateful to have married him.

lessons.title: Make the home a place without noise and fatigue
lessons.body: Let the trials happen outside, but the home should be a safe, peaceful zone and not a source of friction.

lessons.title: One bad moment does not define the whole journey
lessons.body: A last unkind word does not decide years of relationship, and Allah is the Most Merciful.

lessons.title: Be faithful to a spouse for life
lessons.body: Though polygamy was common then, the Prophet SAW did not marry another while Khadijah lived, and Khadijah never hurt him.

lessons.title: Bring joy to a grieving heart
lessons.body: Reading these stories helps us understand others' grief and help them well, because we all need other people.

glossary.meaning: The year of the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah, followed by the journey to Ta'if; the ustaz describes it in three parts.
Words of comfort and sympathy to a family that has lost someone.
One who dies in the cause of Allah; the ustaz says we may pray for it but cannot be sure someone is a martyr.
The phrase Inna lillahi wa inna ilaihi raji'un, suitable for every situation.
The shunning of Bani Hashim that lasted nearly three years, with food supplies cut off.
Calm, deep love and compassion that form the foundation of a household.
A place in Al-Mu'alla, Makkah, where Khadijah was buried and where the Prophet SAW camped at the conquest of Makkah.
Spring, in the prayer asking for the Quran to be spring for a grieving heart.
Rich, which the ustaz says means having no wants, not merely having much wealth.

dalil.context: It is not for the Prophet and the believers to seek forgiveness for the polytheists even if they are relatives, which is why the Prophet SAW stopped asking forgiveness for Abu Talib after Allah forbade it.
dalil.translation: It is not fitting for the Prophet and the believers to ask forgiveness for the idolaters- even if they are related to them- after having been shown that they are the inhabitants of the Blaze:

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah likens spouses to garments in the Ramadan verses of Surah Al-Baqarah, to nurture love and romance in marriage.
dalil.translation: You [believers] are permitted to lie with your wives during the night of the fast: they are [close] as garments to you, as you are to them. God was aware that you were betraying yourselves, so He turned to you in mercy and pardoned you: now you can lie with them- seek what God has ordained for you- eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct from the black. Then fast until nightfall. Do not lie with them during the nights of your devotional retreat in the mosques: these are the bounds set by God, so do not go near them. In this way God makes His messages clear to people, that they may guard themselves against doing wrong.

dalil.context: The ustaz refers to the word aghna in Surah Ad-Duha, saying richness is having no wants, and the Prophet SAW was made sufficient after being an orphan, a shepherd and marrying Khadijah.
dalil.translation: Did He not find you in need and make you self-sufficient?

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions the three groups first thrown into the Fire: the learned reciter of the Quran, the martyr and the generous, so that we are not overconfident about the Hereafter and always hope for Allah's mercy.
dalil.translation: A martyr will be called and asked what he did. He will say he fought in defence of Allah's religion until he was martyred. Allah will say you lie, you did it so people would call you a martyr, and that has already been given. Then he will be dragged and thrown into the Fire.

dalil.context: Some scholars say this hadith took place not long before Khadijah died. The ustaz explains why noise and fatigue are mentioned: those are what Khadijah bore in this world in defending the Prophet SAW.
dalil.translation: Jibril came to the Prophet SAW and said, O Messenger of Allah, here is Khadijah coming with a vessel holding a dish, food or drink. When she reaches you, give her greetings from her Lord and from me, and give her glad tidings of a house in Paradise made of pearl, with no noise in it and no fatigue. Khadijah replied, Allah is As-Salam, from Him is peace, and upon Jibril be peace.

dalil.context: The ustaz calls this a fairly strong narration and a dialogue that captures the Prophet SAW's grief.
dalil.translation: Khawlah told the Prophet SAW she saw him very sad after Khadijah died. The Prophet SAW replied, yes, she managed all my affairs and she was the one who believed me when people called me a liar. In another version, Khadijah looked after my needs and ran my household.

dalil.context: The ustaz reminds us that the funeral is the most important reminder, yet we are distracted by phones and selfies.
dalil.translation: Death is what cuts off all the pleasures of this world.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW wore a fine garment from Yemen and the Companions praised it, and he remembered Sa'ad bin Mu'adh, whose death shook the Throne and whose funeral was escorted by 70,000 angels.
dalil.translation: The handkerchief of Sa'ad bin Mu'adh in Paradise is far better than this garment.

dalil.context: The woman was named Jathamah Al-Muzaniyah and the Prophet SAW changed her name to Hassanah. The ustaz asks us to keep ties with friends and family of those we love who are gone.
dalil.translation: An old woman came and the Prophet SAW asked after her with great care. Aisyah asked why, and the Prophet SAW replied, she used to visit us in the time of Khadijah. Keeping faith with old ties is part of faith.

dalil.context: The Prophet SAW's face changed as it did when revelation came or when he saw dark clouds and an eclipse. Aisyah told the story so that we may learn how the Prophet loved and was loyal to Khadijah.
dalil.translation: Aisyah said, not one morning did the Prophet SAW go out without mentioning Khadijah, until one day her human jealousy overcame her and she said, why do you keep mentioning that old woman with red gums, when Allah has given you better. The Prophet SAW swore, by Allah, Allah never replaced her with anyone better: she believed in me when others disbelieved, she affirmed me when people called me a liar, she gave me her wealth when others withheld, and Allah gave me children through her and not through other women.

dalil.context: The ustaz highlights the Prophet SAW's reply, which puts himself as the one granted Khadijah's love, though it was Khadijah who was grateful to be married to the Prophet SAW.
dalil.translation: Aisyah said, I was not jealous of any wife of the Prophet except Khadijah, because I never met her. When the Messenger of Allah slaughtered a sheep he would say, send this to the friends of Khadijah. One day I became angry and said, Khadijah has long since turned to dust. The Prophet SAW replied, I have been granted her love.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this hadith briefly at the end because we must understand others' grief and help them well.
dalil.translation: Among the things Allah loves is bringing joy into the heart of someone who is grieving.

sirah.era: The Year of Sorrow, tenth year of prophethood
sirah.summary: After the death of Abu Talib and the end of the boycott, Khadijah RA died in Ramadan of the tenth year of prophethood, and the Prophet SAW bore very heavy grief before the journey to Ta'if.
